evidence.claim: Toro says it offers products through a network of professional distributors, dealers, rental stores, and retailers in more than 125 countries, serving golf courses, contractors, groundskeepers, agriculture, rental companies, government, education, homeowners, and sports venues.

Alta says its branch network sells, rents, and provides parts and service support for material handling, construction, environmental processing, cranes, aerial work platforms, paving/asphalt equipment, and allied products.

Alta's 2025 results release stated total revenue was $1.8 billion and described a strategic reduction of rent-to-sell fleet exposure to focus on core dealership capabilities and asset-light product-support profitability.
evidence.source_title: Alta Equipment Group Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 Financial Results and Provides Adjusted EBITDA Guidance for 2026

evidence.claim: Alta's reported market capitalization was approximately $220 million as of the latest finance snapshot, making it a below-USD-300M speculative exception for this funnel.

Titan Machinery describes itself as operating more than 100 full-service agricultural and construction equipment dealer locations across North America, Europe, and Australia, representing CNH Industrial brands and specialty equipment partners.

Titan's fiscal 2026 10-K summary reported revenue streams from equipment, parts, service, and rental/other; parts were $428.3 million and service was $177.9 million for the year ended January 31, 2026.
Titan's reported market capitalization was approximately $435 million as of the latest finance snapshot, placing it in the preferred USD 300M-1B discovery range.

Alamo Group says it is a global manufacturer of more than 40 brands providing industrial and vegetation management equipment for infrastructure and land maintenance, including roadway maintenance, vegetation and tree care, snow and ice control, and public works.
Alamo's 2025 10-K reported total net sales of $1.604 billion, including $654.1 million in Vegetation Management and $949.7 million in Industrial Equipment.
Alamo's reported market capitalization was approximately $1.87 billion as of the latest finance snapshot.
Toro's reported market capitalization was approximately $8.95 billion as of the latest finance snapshot.

memory_update.text: TTC should be retained as a reference benchmark for professional dealer/distributor/rental-channel equipment exposure tied to landscaping, turf, irrigation, and specialty construction.

ALTG is an unusually direct but speculative-shadow candidate for the node because it is a public equipment dealership platform with branch density, OEM relationships, parts/service support, and used/rental equipment channels, but market cap is below the preferred USD 300M floor.
TITN fits the underfollowed discovery lane: small-cap public CNH dealership network with visible parts and service revenue streams and local full-service equipment support.

ALG is a second-order equipment manufacturer candidate where the key research gap is whether spare parts, wear parts, dealer/distribution breadth, and installed-base service economics are material enough to support the chokepoint thesis.

Need a follow-up Layer 1C/2 evidence pass on aftermarket revenue disclosure, dealer exclusivity, technician density, parts inventory availability, used-equipment resale values, and OEM agreement durability for ALTG, TITN, ALG, and TTC.

node: Dealer, service, spare-parts, and resale networks for consumer-adjacent equipment
summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around public companies whose consumer-discretionary or consumer-infrastructure exposure is indirect: equipment fleets, contractor tools, landscaping/grounds equipment, construction equipment, material handling, spare parts, and service density. The strongest direct fit is not consumer brands, but equipment manufacturers and dealership platforms where local support, parts availability, trained operators, used-equipment liquidity, and OEM authorization can create hard-to-replicate distribution moats. This pass includes one reference leader and three underfollowed small/mid or speculative-shadow names. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
